title: Cross-Border Ephemeral Access Orchestration and Evidence Playbook
author: Morgan Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard for orchestrating short-lived (ephemeral) privileges in cross-border and multi-region contexts, and for assembling verifiable audit evidence for compliance reviews and incident response. It bridges RBAC policies, audit logging schema, data residency controls, secure-SDLC gate integration, and incident-response evidence packaging so that short-lived credential flows remain auditable, locality-aware, and defensible for external auditors.

Scope:
- Applies to any automation or human workflow that issues ephemeral credentials (STS tokens, short-lived service accounts, ephemeral SSH certs, signed URLs) that grant access to production inference, model artifacts, or telemetry containing customer data.
- Covers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments where cross-region or cross-border access may be requested.
- Does not replace per-customer contractual residency constraints; it operationalizes evidence for those constraints.

Goals and success criteria:
- Every ephemeral grant must be correlated to a single approval record and a single audit traceable by a unique correlation_id.
- Audit evidence package for any grant must be reconstructible within 4 hours and exportable within 24 hours for legal/compliance review.
- No ephemeral grant should bypass residency-preserving controls for regulated customers (e.g., EU/UK/CA/PAC).

Definitions:
- Ephemeral credential: Any credential with TTL <= 24 hours used to access production systems or customer data.
- Correlation_id: A UUID assigned at the time of request that links request, approval, issuance, activity logs, and revocation artifacts.
- Evidence bundle: Zipped set of logs, approval records, signed statements, and metadata manifest sufficient for audit.

Ownership and roles:
- Access Governance Owner: Security - Morgan Chen. Responsible for policy, exceptions, and training.
- Credential Broker Service Owner: Eng Infra - Priya Natarajan. Responsible for issuance pipeline and enforcement hooks.
- Oncall Incident Lead: Eng SRE - designated in the runbook. Responsible for triage and evidence delivery.
- Customer Privacy Liaison: Legal/Privacy - Jamal Ortiz. Approves residency exceptions.

Policy (high level):
1) Approval first: All ephemeral grants require an approval flow captured in the Access Governance system before issuance. Approved channels: console canary, ticketing system with templated approval, or pre-authorized automation with policy.
2) Minimal privilege: Issue only the least-privileged role and for the shortest TTL compatible with the task.
3) Residency constraints: If the resource or customer has data residency requirements, issuance must preserve data locality (no cross-region egress).
4) Evidence linkage: Every grant must include correlation_id that is propagated to downstream RPCs and emitted in logs.

Technical Controls and Enforcement:
- Credential Broker: Centralized service that signs and mint ephemeral tokens. Enforces TTL caps by role and region. It emits an issuance event to the Audit Stream with the correlation_id.
- Policy Engine: OPA-based evaluation with residency-aware plugins. Evaluates whether issuance would violate residency or compliance contracts.
- Request header propagation: SDKs and edge-proxies must inject X-Redwood-Correlation: <correlation_id>. This is enforced by a gateway sidecar in private deployments.
- Automatic revocation: TTL-backed and manual revocation endpoints that remove active sessions and rotate in-memory secrets when a revocation is recorded.

Audit Logging Schema (example fields; required):
- log_timestamp (ISO8601)
- correlation_id (uuid)
- event_type (issuance|approval|access|revocation|evidence_export)
- principal (service_account|user:<email>|automation:<name>)
- resource_id (model:<name>|endpoint:<id>|artifact:<sha256>)
- region (us-west-2|eu-west-1|ap-southeast-1)
- residency_tag (none|EU_ONLY|CA_ONLY|CUSTOMER_ZONE:<id>)
- policy_decision (allow|deny|conditional)
- raw_request (base64-encoded JSON)
- request_headers (headers JSON; must include X-Redwood-Correlation)
- outcome (success|failure)
- reason (free text)

Example audit entry (JSON blob for logging pipeline):
{
  "log_timestamp": "2026-03-09T15:24:08Z",
  "correlation_id": "a1f9c2b8-7f45-4a3d-9c6d-2f98e5b2d111",
  "event_type": "issuance",
  "principal": "user:maria.gonzalez@redwood.ai",
  "resource_id": "endpoint:prod-translate-1",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "residency_tag": "EU_ONLY",
  "policy_decision": "allow",
  "raw_request": "eyJ0YXNrIjoiZ3JhbnQifQ==",
  "request_headers": "{\"X-Redwood-Correlation\":\"a1f9c2b8-7f45-4a3d-9c6d-2f98e5b2d111\"}",
  "outcome": "success",
  "reason": "approved-by:approver@redwood.ai via ticket #3421"
}

Evidence Packaging and Export (required artifacts):
- Signed approval record (PDF/JSON) with approver identity and timestamp.
- Issuance event and TTL metadata from Credential Broker.
- All access logs correlated to correlation_id for the grant window (start to revocation/expiry).
- Policy decisions and OPA trace for the request.
- Residency constraint resolution artifacts (decision, KMS region used, storage region).
- Manifest.json describing files, hashes, and signing keys.
- Digital signature over the manifest produced by Security key (HSM-backed).

Evidence assembly command (operator-friendly):
1) Retrieve correlation_id: export CORR_ID=a1f9c2b8-7f45-4a3d-9c6d-2f98e5b2d111
2) Run bundler: 
   redwood-audit-cli bundle --correlation $CORR_ID --from "2026-03-09T15:00:00Z" --to "2026-03-09T16:00:00Z" --out /tmp/evidence-$CORR_ID.zip
3) Validate signature: redwood-audit-cli verify /tmp/evidence-$CORR_ID.zip --trusted-keys /etc/security/trusted-keys.pem

Decision tree (short):
- Is the principal in an approved group? If no -> block.
- Does the resource have residency_tag != none? If yes -> is issuance region matched? If no -> deny and escalate to Legal.
- Is TTL request <= role cap? If no -> reduce TTL or require second-level approval.

Playbook: Issuance, Detection, and Revocation (step-by-step)
1) Requester opens a ticket or console request. System assigns correlation_id and starts approval workflow.
2) Approver reviews the request; approver records decision in the Access Governance system. Approval record includes approver, business justification, and residency checks.
3) Credential Broker polls approvals, attempts issuance only if policy engine allows. It emits issuance audit event.
4) User/service uses credentials; all calls include correlation_id which is logged by gateway and downstream services.
5) Automated monitors trigger if anomalous access pattern appears (thresholds below). If triggered, SRE oncall receives alert with correlation_id.
6) Oncall executes rapid revocation: redwood-credentials revoke --correlation $CORR_ID; and runs evidence bundler.
7) Incident lead assembles evidence bundle, signs manifest, and notifies Legal and Customer Privacy Liaison if customer data is involved.

Anomaly thresholds (examples):
- Access rate > 5x baseline for a correlation_id in a 1-minute window.
- Token used from >3 distinct regions within TTL.
- Large-volume artifact downloads > 100MB within 10 minutes against model artifacts tagged CUSTOMER_SENSITIVE.

Incident integration and SLA:
- Time-to-detect target: 5 minutes for high-severity unusual-access alerts.
- Time-to-revoke target: 10 minutes from alert to revocation for high-severity incidents.
- Evidence assembly SLA: 4 hours for initial bundle, 24 hours for full signed bundle to Legal.

Secure-SDLC gates and automation:
- Any code that modifies Credential Broker, sidecar injection, or gateway must include tests that assert correlation_id propagation in unit and integration tests.
- Pull requests changing TTL caps must include a Security README describing rationale and a small attack-surface assessment.
- Release pipeline emits a pre-deploy checklist confirming residency-aware policy tests passed for regions affected.

Data residency special cases and exceptions:
- Temporary exception to cross-region issuance requires Legal pre-approval and must be recorded as an exception with expiry. Exception metadata becomes part of evidence bundle.
- For Private deployments that are air-gapped, local credential brokers must be configured to never issue cross-border tokens; automated unit tests enforce that.

Evidence retention and archival:
- Evidence bundles are stored for a minimum of 7 years for regulated customers, 2 years for general infra. Storage is region-tagged and encrypted with KMS keys that correspond to the residency_tag.
- Index metadata (correlation_id, principal, small set of fields) stored in central index for 10 years for searchability; index excludes raw request payloads for privacy.

Operational runbooks (quick commands):
- Force revoke by correlation_id:
  redwood-credentials revoke --correlation a1f9c2b8-7f45-4a3d-9c6d-2f98e5b2d111 --reason "suspected-exfil"
- Export evidence for compliance:
  redwood-audit-cli bundle --correlation a1f9c2b8-7f45-4a3d-9c6d-2f98e5b2d111 --out ./evidence.zip --signed-by /etc/security/key.pem

Monitoring and metrics to track:
- Issuance per hour per region (trend)
- Percentage of issuance with approval record present (target 100%)
- Time to evidence bundle assembly (p95 < 4h)
- Frequency of revocation actions and average time-to-revoke

Training and audit cadence:
- Quarterly tabletop exercises with SRE, Security, Legal, and Product regarding ephemeral credential incidents.
- Annual external audit of the evidence packaging process for customers with contractual residency requirements.

  "files": ["approval.json","issuance.log","access-logs.jsonl","opa-trace.json"],

}
